skill.description: Use picocom and a Python serial helper to connect to IoT UART consoles, monitor serial output, run authorized commands, and document embedded-device security tests.
skill.summary: Connect to IoT UART consoles with picocom for authorized embedded-device security testing.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed that many high and critical findings are real in context: the skill includes root shell, authentication bypass, persistence, credential discovery, firmware dumping, and transfer workflows. Several scanner hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, serial device paths, reference links, timestamped log names, and benign local setup commands. The helper also exposes shell=True trigger execution and stores serial logs that may contain secrets.

remediation.issue: Persistence and backdoor procedures are documented as actionable steps.
remediation.suggestion: Remove backdoor-user, reverse-shell, startup persistence, and unauthorized SSH access instructions. Replace them with detection-only guidance and explicit authorization checks.

remediation.issue: Bootloader examples show authentication bypass and root shell access.
remediation.suggestion: Gate destructive or bypass-oriented bootloader steps behind clear lab-only warnings and require user approval before any state-changing command.

remediation.issue: Monitor mode executes trigger_script with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True, parse trigger commands into argv arrays, or restrict triggers to an allowlist of approved local commands.

remediation.issue: Firmware dumping examples include network transfer of root filesystem images.
remediation.suggestion: Frame firmware extraction as authorized evidence handling, remove attacker-host examples, and require secure storage and transfer instructions.

remediation.issue: Default examples store sensitive serial logs under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use a protected log directory with restrictive permissions, warn before logging secrets, and document secure cleanup.

content.user_title: Audit IoT UART Consoles with picocom
content.value_statement: Embedded device testing often requires reliable serial console access and careful session capture. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through authorized picocom workflows with structured logging.
actual_capabilities: Connects to USB serial devices through picocom or the included Python helper.
Sends single commands, batch command files, or interactive serial input.
Monitors passive UART output and compares baseline and triggered device logs.
Supports AT command interfaces for modems and GPS modules.
Documents bootloader, shell, enumeration, and firmware analysis workflows.
Captures serial sessions to log files for later review.
limitations: Requires physical UART access and correct serial wiring.
Assumes picocom and pyserial are installed on the host system.
Can execute commands on connected devices and must be used only with authorization.
Session logs may contain sensitive credentials or device identifiers.

use_cases.title: Validate UART Access
use_cases.description: Connect to a lab device, identify the prompt, and confirm reliable command output.

use_cases.title: Capture Boot Diagnostics
use_cases.description: Record boot logs from an embedded device and compare output before and after a controlled trigger.

use_cases.title: Document Authorized Findings
use_cases.description: Collect serial evidence, command results, and device context for a security assessment report.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Serial Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a known UART adapter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the picocom skill to connect to /dev/ttyUSB0 at 115200 baud. Log the session and identify the device prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Enumerate a Lab Device
prompt_templates.scenario: Collect basic information after authorized shell access.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the serial helper to run a safe enumeration plan on my authorized test device. Summarize the firmware, network, and process information you observe.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor Triggered Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare UART logs around a controlled external action.
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor the UART console for 60 seconds, capture a baseline, run the approved trigger command, and report new log lines after the trigger.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Bootloader Exposure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of bootloader behavior in a controlled lab.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the authorized bootloader session. Identify risky settings, explain impact, and avoid changes unless I explicitly approve them.

output_examples.input: Connect to a UART adapter and identify the console state.
output_examples.output: The session opened at 115200 baud, the prompt was detected, and the device returned a BusyBox-style shell banner.

output_examples.input: Monitor boot logs while a test device reboots.
output_examples.output: The capture separated baseline, reboot, and post-reboot messages. It highlighted kernel version, mounted storage, and one failed service start.
The report lists firmware identifiers, active network interfaces, running services, and follow-up checks that require user approval.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization before connecting to a device or sending commands.
Use dedicated lab hardware and keep serial logs in a protected directory.
Review every command before it changes boot settings, credentials, or firmware.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill on third-party devices without explicit permission.
Do not leave serial logs with passwords or keys in shared temporary directories.
Do not run persistence, backdoor, or firmware-writing steps during routine diagnostics.

faq.question: What hardware is required?
faq.answer: You need a UART adapter, correct wiring, and permission to test the target device.

faq.question: Can it work without picocom?
faq.answer: The helper script can use pyserial directly, but the skill also documents picocom workflows.

faq.question: Does it support AT commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper includes an AT mode for devices that respond with OK or ERROR status lines.

faq.question: Where are logs stored?
faq.answer: Examples often use temporary paths, but sensitive sessions should use a protected directory.

faq.question: Is this safe for production devices?
faq.answer: Use caution. Serial commands can change device state, expose secrets, or interrupt normal operation.

faq.question: Why is authorization important?
faq.answer: The skill includes security testing workflows that can bypass controls or access sensitive data.
